sections.html:
Sumter County fills about 682 square miles of the state's midlands. Its seat, the city of Sumter, is also the largest town: 43,463 people lived there in 2020, against 105,556 countywide. The Wateree River runs along the western line, the Black River drains much of the land, and Lake Marion is one of the area's big waters.

A house near the Wateree, the Black River or the lake deserves a flood map check early. Mortgage lenders always run one.

Shaw Air Force Base is the name everyone knows, and families stationed there sometimes must sell in a hurry when orders shift. Manufacturing is the largest job sector, at about 18 percent. Old deeds can be awkward. Ground that once sat in Clarendon County may have its records under that county's name, so family land calls for a title search.

The Assessor and the Treasurer work out of one building at 13 East Canal Street, Sumter, SC 29150. Hours run 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday. Dial 803-436-2102 for the county switchboard or 803-436-2213 for delinquent taxes.

If one number rings out, try the other and ask for the Treasurer.

In short, one office decides what your property is worth and how it is classed, another takes exemption applications, and the Treasurer takes the payment. Have your parcel number ready, since each desk asks for it up front. Staff can often point you to the right form on the spot, and a short call saves a wasted trip downtown.

Bills are mailed in October and carry no extra charge until after January 15. Options include the county's qpaybill website, the mail, or a visit to the office.

Web screens may omit penalties and fees. Confirm the full amount with the Treasurer before paying late or closing a sale.

State law allows a county council to permit installments through an ordinance. Ask the Treasurer if Sumter County does before planning to split a bill.

Your primary home is assessed at 4 percent of its value, while second homes and rentals are assessed at 6 percent. Request the lower rate from the Assessor right after moving in, and report a change within 30 days if you stop living there. Being misclassed at 6 percent costs money every year.

  • A reassessment can raise your taxable value by no more than 15 percent.
  • A mailed notice follows any rise in fair market value of $1,000 or more.
  • Homestead exemption: an owner aged 65 or over, totally disabled or legally blind, with a year of state residency, shields the first $50,000 of the home's value. The County Auditor's Office takes the application.
  • Disabled ex-service members and surviving spouses of those killed in the line of duty may qualify for an exemption on the home and up to five acres, handled through the SC Department of Revenue.

The Assessor can tell you the date of the next countywide reassessment.

Put your objection in writing to the County Assessor no later than 90 days after the notice date. Waiting for the tax bill isn't required.

  1. An appeal still pending on December 31 means a bill of at least 80 percent of current assessed value.
  2. Asking in writing to be billed above 80 percent limits interest if you lose.
  3. The January 15 due date stays.
  4. Once the appeal is decided, you receive a refund or owe the difference with interest.

Appeals of Department of Revenue assessments run on a separate track with their own 90-day protest rule.

Real estate and mobile home taxes left unpaid are swept into the delinquent tax sale. The Treasurer has announced December 8, 2026 as this year's date. Pay everything by 5 p.m. on December 7, 2026 and the property comes off the list. Call 803-436-2213 to verify, since dates shift.

A sold property can be bought back within 12 months under state law. The interest owed grows through the year, at 3, 6, 9 or 12 percent, depending on the quarter you redeem in. Certified mail warns the owner between 45 and 20 days before the window shuts.

Request a written payoff including penalties, and note how close the sale date is. Confirm your home carries the 4 percent classification and correct it if not. When a reappraisal notice has arrived, set the contract price against the new assessment, because a big gap could justify an appeal.

The closing agent deducts any unpaid tax from your proceeds, leaving the buyer clean title. Title companies ask for the number early, so call the Treasurer first. With an inherited house, confirm the seller is the person named on the title.

Our company purchases Sumter County homes in any condition, even ones behind on taxes or passed down in an estate. Tell us the address and the amount owed, and we will describe how a cash sale would go.

Think of the tax year as a calendar you can plan around. Bills appear in October, the penalty-free window closes January 15, and charges grow on February 1 and again after March 16. A house sold early in the year may still owe a bill from the year before, which is why the Treasurer's payoff matters more than the paper notice in your drawer.

If you are weighing a listing against a cash offer, count the months. A traditional sale can run past the point where penalties begin, while a quick closing lets the payoff come straight out of the proceeds. Whichever route you pick, nothing transfers cleanly until the balance is cleared and the deed is recorded.

Owners who inherited a house should also check whether the bill is still mailed to the previous owner. Send the Assessor and Treasurer your current mailing address in writing so notices stop going astray. If a notice never arrives, the tax and its penalties still apply, so don't wait for the mail to remind you.

Carry your newest tax notice, parcel number and photo ID. A homestead or residence claim goes better with proof of age or disability and proof that you live in the home. An appeal needs the assessment notice plus backup for your figure, like recent sales of comparable houses nearby. When a deadline looms, a written request beats a phone call.

Keep copies of whatever you submit, and write down the date and the clerk who helped.

faqs.q: When are Sumter County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The deadline without penalty is January 15. Charges then step up to 3 percent, 10 percent after February 1 and 15 percent after March 16.

faqs.q: When is the Sumter County tax sale?
faqs.a: December 8, 2026 is the date announced by the Treasurer. Payment by 5 p.m. on December 7 keeps a property out of it. Check at 803-436-2213.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Sumter County assessment?
faqs.a: Ninety days, counted from the notice date. Write to the Assessor, and still pay on time because an appeal doesn't postpone the due date.

faqs.q: What is the legal residence rate in Sumter County?
faqs.a: Your own home is assessed at 4 percent and other residential property at 6 percent. The Assessor processes the application.

faqs.q: Can I get the homestead exemption in Sumter County?
faqs.a: Yes, when you are 65 or older, totally disabled or legally blind and have lived in South Carolina a year. The first $50,000 of value is excluded, and you apply at the County Auditor's Office.
